question: Should generic `tool-progress` intent become a permanent public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract for bundled and third-party plugins?
rationale: The bug can be fixed with typed producer intent, but exporting the constant and predicate commits OpenClaw to an additive third-party API that automation cannot approve on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Approve the generic contract
options.body: Keep the additive generic constant and predicate as the canonical way for plugins to identify transient tool progress, then require exact-head Slack proof.

options.title: Keep the intent internal
options.body: Replace the public exports with a narrower internal or injected runtime seam while preserving the same Slack behavior.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers do not want a new progress-intent API and no suitably narrow seam is available.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic contract
recommendation.body: Keep the additive generic constant and predicate as the canonical way for plugins to identify transient tool progress, then require exact-head Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history owns the Slack native-data delivery architecture and adjacent Plugin SDK boundary decisions most directly affected here.
